teaching.hint: Where must the smaller member of a fixed-product pair lie, and how does its choice affect the gap?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: For a fixed positive product P, restrict the smaller factor to at most sqrt(P); its gap P/a-a decreases as a increases.
solution_outline.approach: For each permitted product, search downward from its integer square root until a divisor is found. Pair it with the quotient and choose the smaller gap between the two products.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The first divisor encountered is the largest divisor no greater than the square root; all larger candidate smaller factors have already been ruled out.
solution_outline.correctness: Every positive factor pair can be oriented with its smaller factor at most sqrt(P). On that domain, increasing a reduces P/a while increasing a itself, so the gap strictly decreases. The first divisor below the root therefore gives the optimal pair for P. Comparing the two allowed products is exhaustive.
solution_outline.pitfall: Testing divisors of num itself solves a different problem; preserve the two allowed products and exact square-root boundary.

source_fidelity_notes: Specified positive factors as used throughout the canonical explanation and examples; retained either-product choice, any-order output, and bounds.
common_wrong_turns: Testing divisors of num itself solves a different problem; preserve the two allowed products and exact square-root boundary.
